_: Sub-lake areas a regulation names and the atlas cannot draw. Each `area` is the book's OWN words for a part of a lake — an arm, a bay, the water inside a line between boundary signs — and each needs a polygon before the rule it serves can bind to anything. Until one exists the rule is carried on the whole lake, unplaced and marked, never widened to it. `polygon: null` is the worklist; fill it with a ring in EPSG:4326 and the rule binds. Generated from the shipped bundle as a ROSTER; the polygons themselves are hand work. Kootenay Lake is listed first: its areas come from a zone entry with no item of its own, which the roster's own query could not see, so that shape is a known gap in the sweep rather than an absence of cases.

lakes.note: THE HARD CASE. The book divides this lake into three named areas — Main Body, Upper West Arm, Lower West Arm — in a zone entry that belongs to no registry item, because a definition is not a rule. Two real rules then name one of those areas: the annual rainbow quota and the Kootenay rainbow stamp, both Main Body only. Until the three polygons exist, neither can bind to a part of the lake, and both are carried on the whole of it, unplaced.
